A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAGE research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original WOMD/MetaDrive experiments on adversarial generation, closed-loop driving-policy training, preference interpolation, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds GOOSE comparisons, cross-generator policy evaluation, reward-margin sensitivity results, and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: The HGPO pairing rules and loss, two preference experts, weight interpolation and extrapolation, and dual-axis curriculum are unchanged. Sections 3 and B and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedures; expanded implementation descriptions do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use WOMD scenarios in MetaDrive and the Replay, RL, IDM, and Autopilot ego policies. CAT- and Rule-generated environments already occur in v1. The new cross-evaluation recombines retained generators and trained policies within this coverage.

E2.justification: GOOSE becomes an evaluated baseline in v2 Tables 1, 2, 8, and 9, whereas v1 only cites its paper. Rule, CAT, KING, AdvTrajOpt, SEAL, and the existing mixing and closed-loop training comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds held-out cross-evaluation of four trained policies in CAT- and Rule-generated environments and a reward-margin sweep over 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1, and 2. Existing splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged; newly specified baseline objectives are implementation disclosures.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially: Table 4 tests generator-specific overfitting, Figure 10 examines reward-margin sensitivity, and Figures 3, 8, and 12 add behavioral diversity, baseline failure, and reactive-policy cases. The original component ablations and extrapolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing ± summaries and shaded training curves are retained, and new Table 4 follows the same reporting convention. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, or an explanation of the reported uncertainty quantities.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results from GOOSE, cross-generator evaluation, and margin sensitivity. In new Table 4, SAGE has the highest reported completion rates, 0.678 and 0.655; CAT and Rule training achieve the lowest collision rates in their respective environments. These are added findings, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The existing theorems, bounds, and Proposition 1 formula remain. Section 3.4 and Appendix C.3 revise the flatness-based reasoning, and new Remark 1 derives Equation 58 under local quadratic and Jacobian approximations, requiring loss curvature to exceed directional output sensitivity.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about preference alignment, hierarchical feasibility handling, test-time control without retraining, LMC justification, and improved closed-loop training. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the flatness explanation with a curvature-dominance interpretation, discusses generator-specific overfitting and SAGE's completion-versus-collision trade-off, and explains reward-margin sensitivity through noisy preferences versus lost training pairs. Existing applicability claims and future directions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds checkpoint provenance, official implementation information, and explicit baseline objectives and reward weights. New Table 7 consolidates existing HGPO settings and discloses batch size and previously unspecified penalty coefficients. These additions improve documentation without demonstrating changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work sections, and novelty positioning remain unchanged. GOOSE's paper was already cited in v1; its new participation in experiments changes the comparison set rather than the literature coverage.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory revisions and an additional case-study subsection, while the principal narrative and section order remain. v2 also updates the publication header, expands acknowledgments, and adds an LLM-use declaration.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 7 and Figures 3, 8, 10, and 12, inserts GOOSE rows, and expands several captions. Existing displays are retained with relocation and renumbering; the overall single-column layout and visual design remain.

improvement.justification: Cross-generator evaluation in Table 4 strengthens the assessment of policy generalization, while Figure 10 and Table 7 improve parameter justification and reproducibility. The revised curvature argument is more precise but remains conditional, without quantitatively verifying Equation 58; uncertainty reporting also remains unexplained. These are useful, limited gains over the retained core method and results.
